questions.question: Define a code of ethics and explain why financial information depends on it.
questions.expected_answer: A code of ethics is a formal, written statement of the values and standards of behaviour a business commits itself to, binding all parties in the financial environment — owners, managers, bookkeepers, employees, and dealings with customers, suppliers and the state. Financial information only has value if it can be trusted: banks, owners and the revenue service all rely on figures being honestly made, so ethics is the precondition of the discipline, not an add-on. Internal control makes dishonesty difficult; ethics makes it unwanted.

questions.question: Apply the four-move method to this scenario: the owner of Mokoena Hardware orders his bookkeeper to leave Saturday cash sales out of the records to reduce tax.
questions.expected_answer: Issue: cash sales are being deliberately excluded from the records to evade tax. Name: this breaches leadership and fairness by the owner (and discipline and accountability if the bookkeeper complies). Argument: leadership fails because dishonesty is ordered from the top; fairness fails because the dodged tax shifts the burden onto honest taxpayers; the records become deliberately incomplete. Consequence and correction: penalties, criminal exposure and lost credibility with the bank; all sales must be recorded and the code of ethics enforced from the owner downward.

questions.question: Explain, with one business example, why good ethics is good business rather than a cost on top of profit.
questions.expected_answer: Each characteristic converts into a business advantage: a salon charging exactly the advertised price wins loyal clients (fairness into loyalty); honest records show a bank what the salon really earns and unlock a loan (transparency into credit); paying suppliers on the agreed date earns credit terms in slow months (discipline into breathing room); treating staff and community well keeps the business standing for years (sustainability into survival). The reverse compounds: one discovered dishonesty makes every past figure suspect, and trust does not restock.
